partner_context.their_ambition: Yango is the Dubai-headquartered global ride-tech platform operating across the Middle East, Africa, the Caspian and South Asia. Critically — and this is the lead frame for every conversation — this is the **Dubai-HQ'd Yango**, headquartered and operationally based in the UAE, with its growth centred on the GCC, Africa and emerging coastal markets. That footprint maps almost perfectly onto the world's most underbuilt waterfronts: lagoon megacities, Gulf jetty networks, Red Sea resorts and Caspian bays where the road is congested and the water is empty.

hero.title: Yango × Navier — the water tier for the Dubai-HQ'd global ride platform
hero.subtitle: From Dubai's jetties to Lagos's lagoon and the Caspian shore — a foiling water tier in the Yango app.
hero.what_we_do_together: A Yango-branded electric-foiling water-mobility tier across Yango's strongest markets — anchored in its home UAE, spanning African lagoon megacities (Lagos, Abidjan, Dakar), the GCC (Qatar, Saudi commercial), Türkiye's Bosphorus and Aegean, Egypt's Red Sea and Nile, and the Caspian — booked in the same Yango app, on the same wallet, as the car.

why_now: Yango is scaling aggressively beyond ride-hailing into a multimodal super-app, exactly as Navier's N30 Pioneer II becomes commercially available. Yango's geography is uniquely water-shaped: Dubai (its HQ) has the densest luxury-jetty network on earth; Lagos, Abidjan and Dakar are lagoon-and-island megacities choked by bridges; the Bosphorus is the world's busiest commuter strait; the Red Sea and Caspian are building marine-first tourism. Pioneer II is commercial now and clears the dense short-water corridors across all of them, with Quanta-LR staged honestly for the longer regional legs.

network_thesis.headline: Yango water network
network_thesis.body: Yango's water network shares one global corridor registry with the other partners — the same canonical geometry, country tags and boarding points — but renders as Yango's own branded view with its own economics. Where corridors overlap with another partner (the UAE jetties, Doha Bay, the Jeddah/Red Sea coast), Yango inherits the shared canonical routes rather than recreating them; where Yango is alone (the African lagoons, the Caspian), it extends the shared registry. This is hub-and-spoke at platform scale: one home-market flagship (UAE) proving the model, then a deliberate spoke-by-spoke rollout across Africa, the GCC, Türkiye, Egypt and the Caspian.

multimodal_fit: Same Yango app, same wallet, same account: a Yango car to the jetty, a foiling hop across the bay or lagoon, a Yango ride on arrival. In Yango's home UAE and across its African strongholds, the multimodal water leg is frequently the fastest part of the journey — and it never leaves the Yango ecosystem.
differentiation: Against Yango's incumbent competitors, a foiling water tier is a category nobody else offers — a defensible, premium, all-electric mode on exactly the congested-bridge and slow-ferry corridors where Yango's markets hurt most. Against the diesel ferries and water taxis it replaces: faster, quiet, low-wake, zero-local-emission and on-demand. Against road: a direct line that skips the gridlock.

proof_points.claim: Yango is Dubai-HQ'd with its strongest base in the UAE.
proof_points.evidence: The UAE is both Yango's headquarters and the world's densest premium water-mobility market — the natural home-market flagship.

proof_points.claim: Yango's African footprint is lagoon-and-island shaped.
proof_points.evidence: Lagos (lagoon), Abidjan (Ébrié Lagoon, proven bateaux-bus demand), Dakar (Gorée/island runs) and Maputo Bay are all water-natural megacities where Yango already operates ridehail.

proof_points.claim: The corridors are real, range-gated and shared.
proof_points.evidence: 183 modeled corridors across 15 countries, sharing canonical geometry with the broader partner network and inheriting correct country tags.

proof_points.claim: Vessel sizing is honest by leg.
proof_points.evidence: Every corridor is range-gated — ≤70nm on commercial-now Pioneer II, 75–150nm on roadmap Quanta-LR, longer legs rendered aspirational — never a long leg faked on a short-range boat.

phases.narrative: Launch the dense intra-Dubai jetty network in Yango's home market on Pioneer II, alongside a first proven African lagoon anchor (Lagos or Abidjan). Prove economics where willingness-to-pay is highest and demand is densest.
phases.rationale: Anchor on the home-market flagship and a proven lagoon-commute base before spreading; highest-density, lowest-friction water.

phases.label: Phase 2 — Scale (Africa + GCC + Türkiye + Egypt, N30 + N35)
phases.narrative: Replicate the proven playbook across the African lagoon megacities (Lagos, Abidjan, Dakar, Maputo), the GCC (Doha Bay, Jeddah/Red Sea commercial), the Istanbul Bosphorus and İzmir/Aegean, and Egypt's Red Sea and Nile — adding the N35 Shuttle on the densest corridors to roughly double throughput per hull.

phases.narrative: Open the Quanta-LR regional and trans-water legs (Dubai–Abu Dhabi already in Pioneer range, the giga-project coast, the Caspian and Aegean crossings staged honestly), reach the Caspian markets (Baku, Aktau), and mature into induced demand and full in-app the standard-operator role across the network.
phases.rationale: Honest long-range staging plus Navier becoming the standard operator and earning ride revenue once the dense network is proven; held/sovereign markets (Israel) remain data-only until coordination clears.

the_ask: Co-launch a Yango-branded foiling water tier — anchor in Yango's home UAE with a 3-boat Pioneer II flagship across Dubai's jetties, prove a first African lagoon market in parallel, then roll out spoke-by-spoke across Africa, the GCC, Türkiye, Egypt and the Caspian on the shared corridor network.
close: Yango's Dubai-HQ'd, Africa-and-GCC-heavy footprint is the best-shaped ride-platform geography in the world for water mobility: its busiest markets are lagoon megacities, Gulf jetty networks and congested straits where a foiling tier is both a category nobody else has and the fastest leg of the journey. The home market proves it; the network scales it.
end_state: A Yango water tier spanning its home UAE flagship, the African lagoon megacities, the GCC, the Türkiye straits and Aegean, Egypt's Red Sea and Nile, and the Caspian — one shared corridor network, rendered as Yango's branded view, booked in the Yango app.

objections.objection: Our riders take cars, not boats. Is there really demand on the water?
objections.response: In Yango's own markets the water is already a daily commute — the Suomenlinna ferry in Helsinki, the Maputo–Catembe crossing, the Keamari–Manora launches in Karachi, the Rosario Islands boats out of Cartagena. We add a faster, quieter, premium tier on lines people already ride, and surface it in the same Yango app and wallet.

objections.objection: Won't building jetties and charging cost a fortune before we see revenue?
objections.response: Almost every corridor uses existing quays, ferry piers and marina berths — the boarding points are already there. The N30 is all-electric and charges from berth pedestals, so there is no new fuel or heavy shore infrastructure to stand up before launch.

objections.objection: The distances look long on a map — can an electric boat actually cover them?
objections.response: Every corridor is matched to a hull by distance. Short city and bay legs run on the N30 Pioneer II today; the few long runs (a Sognefjord express, an Aktau–Kuryk coastal line) are flagged as longer-range roadmap legs, never faked on the short-range boat.

objections.objection: Yango is a Russian-linked brand — is that a regulatory risk for this?
objections.response: This is the Dubai-headquartered Yango, operated independently for its international markets. We lead every market engagement with that split, and we keep any sovereign-coordination markets explicitly flagged rather than launching into them.

objections.objection: Some of these coastlines are open ocean with real surf and weather.
objections.response: We are honest about it. Where a shore is exposed — Lima's Costa Verde, Accra's Atlantic beach, Colombo's ocean front — we build on the sheltered water instead (the harbour behind San Lorenzo, the Negombo lagoon, the Ébrié lagoon) and weather-gate the exposed legs. Null beats a route we can't run.

objections.objection: How is this different from the diesel ferries and water taxis already there?
objections.response: Faster on the foils, silent, low-wake and zero local emission, booked on demand in the Yango app — a premium category none of the incumbents offer, on exactly the congested-bridge and slow-ferry corridors where Yango's markets hurt most.

why_navier_now: Navier's N30 Pioneer II is commercially available now, and Yango is expanding into precisely the water-shaped geographies where it fits best — the Gulf's jetty networks, West Africa's lagoon megacities, the Caspian's tideless bays, and Norway's fjords. Moving first gives Yango a premium water tier no competitor offers, on corridors that already carry daily boat traffic, before anyone else claims the category.
coverage_note: Yango's water footprint has been deepened across its full operating map: the Gulf (Oman's Musandam fjords, Bahrain, Qatar, the Eastern Province), West Africa's lagoon megacities (Dakar, Abidjan, Accra, Lagos, Luanda), East Africa (Maputo), South Asia (Karachi, Colombo), the Caribbean and Pacific coasts of Latin America (Cartagena, Barranquilla, Callao), the Caspian (Baku, Aktau), and the Nordic archipelago and fjords (Helsinki, Bergen, Stavanger, Geiranger). Each market is rooted in real waterfronts, existing boarding points and sourced boat-traffic precedents, and matched to the right Navier hull by distance.
